title: Using Human-LLM Disagreement to Improve Checklist-Based Quality Appraisal

live_model.evidence: "item-level agreement between human experts and multiple LLMs (GPT-5-mini-2025-08-07 (OpenAI, 2025)...)"; Figure 5: mean item-level accuracy on the GRoLTS v1 PTSD checklist, gpt-5-mini=0.75.

prompt.location: Sec "Prompt Construction"; full code/prompts released at github.com/timovdk/grolts-llm
prompt.note: RAG pipeline: GRoLTS checklist question + retrieved evidence chunk -> structured binary (yes/no) prompt.

claim.metric: item-level accuracy vs. human labels, GRoLTS v1 checklist (21 binary items), PTSD studies
claim.location: Figure 5 (bottom-row mean accuracy per model); PTSD dataset = 38 previously annotated studies (from the original GRoLTS study, osf.io/vw3t7)

data.source: GRoLTS PTSD dataset (osf.io/vw3t7) plus the paper's own code/outputs, github.com/timovdk/grolts-llm

notes: 38 studies x 21 checklist items = 798 individual yes/no judgments behind the 0.75 mean. A second, larger GRoLTS v2 corpus (Achievement/Delinquency/PTSD, 37 of 65 studies retained) is also evaluated with the same models (Appendix E), giving a second independent claim if needed.
